small_guidance:
- The conv (nn.Conv2d on 128×64×128×128 with 3×3, OC=128) dominates runtime now that InstanceNorm+div is fused; further tuning of the norm kernel (BLOCK/warps/stages sweeps) will yield <5% since it's already memory-bound and fast_p is ~1.03.
- If staying with this structure, try fusing the conv bias add into the instance-norm kernel's first reduction pass (set conv bias=None, pass bias_ptr) to save one full HW read/write per (N,C).
- Consider channels_last memory format for the conv output so subsequent ops coalesce; but main win requires replacing the conv itself.
large_guidance:
- Replace nn.Conv2d with a custom Triton im2col-style GEMM kernel: one program per (N, OC tile, output-spatial tile), implicit im2col gather, BLOCK_M=64/BLOCK_N=64/BLOCK_K=32 starting point, autotune over (64/128, 64/128, 16/32/64) with num_warps 4/8, num_stages 2-3. Input is 128×64×128×128, kernel 3×3, output 128×128×126×126 — large GEMM (K=64*9=576, M=OC=128, N=126*126=15876 per batch) very amenable to a tiled kernel.
- Two-stage fusion strategy: stage 1 = conv (write OC×Hout×Wout per N,C); stage 2 = instance-norm+div as already implemented. Optionally fuse conv bias and (later) a partial-sum/partial-sum-of-squares accumulation across the spatial tile so InstanceNorm stats are accumulated during conv writeout, eliminating one full pass over the conv output.
- Use channels_last layout end-to-end so the GEMM-N axis is contiguous spatial and the IC*kh*kw reduction axis loads coalesce; hoist stride/pad offsets out of the inner K loop and mask the spatial tail.
